title: Lasting aftereffects: music and arranging books sent to the Philippines and Burma
summary: Addie and Jack describe letters, music sent to the Philippines and arranging books sent to Burma.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: For once. But what's capitalism? Well one thing that has carried on from this tour of Asia for instance, that all the boys and myself almost every day we get a letter from someone that we met over there. Jack gets requests for music. He sent a lot of music to the Philippines so they could start some new bands that interest in jazz had pretty much fallen by the wayside in the Philippines until he visited there. Then when we were in Burma, there's a motion picture company there. They had always had to send their scores to Paris to have the picture scored. You know, and have the music written there. And they wanted to learn arranging. So then Jack sent them books on arranging. So when it went back they made quite a ceremony and they were so surprised that we remember them. They think that you've got to forget the day you leave.

Yeah, they sent us pictures in the paper of our American officer presenting these books that I had sent over to them to give to these fellas. They were so good. And they appreciated it so much. So in the long run it did more good than anything that's ever been over.
